frozen_problem.title: Extended-Kruppa constraints, realized conic ambiguity, and invariant eliminants for algebraic silhouettes
frozen_problem.statement: Can we find the fundamental matrix from silhouettes? If the silhouettes are bounded by algebraic curves are there algebraic constraints on the fundamental matrix?
frozen_problem.selection_basis: Rank 19, score 73.5; highest-ranked eligible at freeze outside cooldown and anti-thrashing gates, including the rank-18 packet on open draft PR21. Ranked, not provisional.

theory.target: Audit the quartic invariant eliminant for projective equivalence of squarefree complex binary quartic root divisors, including real-field and repeated-root boundary counterexamples. No silhouette gluing or fundamental-matrix recovery is attempted.
definitions: Root-divisor equivalence allows arbitrary nonzero scalar and PGL2(K) transport, preserving multiplicities.
q_t=XY(X-Y)(X-tY), t in C minus {0,1}; the universal target quantifies over all squarefree complex quartic pairs.
assumptions: Binary quartics use coefficients a,b,c,d,e without binomial scaling.
The completeness claim is over C, for squarefree projective divisors only.
Rational parameters exclude 0 and 1; infinity is retained as a projective root.
Finite census and polynomial identity checks are distinct from independent proof verification.
No geometric realization or surface gluing theorem is established.
approaches_considered: Three-point normalization, exact six-factor identity and the anharmonic cross-ratio orbit.
Field-blind or multiplicity-blind eliminant use, retired by exact counterexamples.
Direct enumeration of projectivities and Sturm chains to discriminate the proposed tests.
falsification_targets: Eliminant zero implies real projective equivalence.
Eliminant zero suffices for nonreduced divisors.
Dividing by I or J is harmless at exceptional quartics.
Quartic divisor matching alone constructs a surface or recovers a fundamental matrix.

claims.statement: Exact eliminant-zero quartics have real-root counts 0 versus 4, and repeated-root controls have multiplicity partitions (4) versus (3,1). These refute weakened tests, not the imported squarefree-complex wording.
claims.falsification_condition: Wrong invariants, real-root count, infinity handling, or multiplicity partition.

claims.statement: The six-factor polynomial identity matches exact sparse expansion; independent algorithms agree on all 2025 rational-parameter pairs, with 213 equivalent pairs and 888 projectivities.
claims.falsification_condition: Any nonzero coefficient residual, omitted parameter or direct-map mismatch.

claims.statement: The ordinary five-step argument gives equivalence of eliminant vanishing and PGL2(C)-equivalence for squarefree quartic root divisors; it remains unverified by an independent author or kernel.
claims.falsification_condition: A squarefree complex counterexample or a gap in normalization, weights, or root-permutation transport.

claims.statement: Fisher v1 Section 2 supplies the unscaled I,J convention and transformation weights; its discriminant is 16 times this packet's D0. It is not evidence of silhouette realization.
claims.falsification_condition: Convention, normalization, field or locator mismatch.

progress.summary: Two exact certificates establish the real-field and multiplicity obstructions to weakened eliminant tests.
Exact polynomial expansion and a 2025-pair census provide a reproducible test of the restricted equivalence criterion.

checks.method: Initial baseline begins with exact Sturm and zero/infinity multiplicity calculations, then reconstructs the census without theory data.
checks.independence_basis: Initial verifier and baseline preceded theory.py. Fresh Python -I with empty environment reconstructs expected results before certificate read. Sturm remainders and 24 ordered projective target triples differ from positivity/sign intervals, sparse polynomial expansion and six-value orbit formulas. Same-assistant authorship and shared specification; no independent human/model/kernel proof review.
checks.result: Real-root counts 0 and 4, partitions (4) and (3,1), and the nonsingular I=0 control all distinguish the boundary cases.

checks.method: Enumerate 24 ordered target triples per pair and evaluate the identity on a degree-sufficient 7x7 grid; compare all output fields and seven mutations.

checks.result: 48600 candidate maps give 213 equivalent pairs and 888 maps; 49 identity grid values agree; seven corrupted outputs rejected; replay unchanged.

progress.summary: Direct projective-map enumeration and Sturm computations independently reproduce the boundary certificates and all finite census data.

unresolved_objections: Same-assistant authorship and shared specification; no independent human/model/kernel proof verification.
The universal complex completeness argument and real-root/multiplicity preservation require independent mathematical review.
Rational census excludes the equianharmonic complex orbit; no inference of exhaustive complex testing.
AIM unavailable; imported status and broader silhouette/gluing claims remain unverified.
No real descent algorithm, surface realization, fundamental-matrix uniqueness, novelty or parent solution claim.

next_step: Obtain independently authored review of the squarefree-complex completeness proof and real descent requirements; separately audit surface-silhouette realization without treating a matching quartic invariant as geometric sufficiency.
